title: Beyond the 956: Dai Henwood, beloved New Zealand comedian, dies at 48
excerpt: Dai Henwood, the New Zealand comedian and television host known for 7 Days, Family Feud, Taskmaster and Dancing with the Stars, has died at 48. He died November 10, 2026, in Auckland Hospital after a six-year battle with colon cancer, his management confirmed.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Dai Henwood, the beloved New Zealand comedian and television host known for 7 Days, Family Feud, Taskmaster and Dancing with the Stars, has died at 48.

Henwood died on the morning of Tuesday, November 10, 2026, at Auckland Hospital, holding the hands of his family, after living with colon cancer for six years. His management, Notorious Comedy, announced the news on Tuesday.

Born Dafydd Morgan Henwood on February 7, 1978, in Wellington, the son of actor Ray Henwood, he built a 27-year comedy career and became a household name in New Zealand through his stand-up, radio and television work, including long-running roles on the comedy panel show 7 Days and as host of New Zealand's Family Feud and Taskmaster.

Henwood was diagnosed with metastatic bowel cancer in 2020 and went public with his diagnosis in January 2023, speaking openly about chemotherapy and his treatment. In 2024 he published the memoir The Life of Dai and shared his cancer journey in the three-part documentary series Live and Let Dai. In June 2025 he was appointed an Officer of the New Zealand Order of Merit for his services to entertainment and charity.

He is survived by his wife Jo, his children Charlie and Lucy, and his mother, Dame Carolyn Henwood. Tributes poured in from across New Zealand, including from former Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern.

Rest in Peace, Dai Henwood.

Sources: NZ Herald; Stuff; Now to Love (statement from his management, Notorious Comedy, November 10, 2026).
